recipes.name: Simple Beef Stroganoff
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can fat-free condensed cream of mushroom soup
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Sauté ground beef in a large skillet over medium heat until browned and crumbly; 5 to 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rapid boil. Cook egg noodles at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, 7 to 9 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Drain and discard any fat from the cooked beef. Stir condensed soup and garlic powder into the beef. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove beef from the heat. Add egg noodles and stir to combine. Stir in sour cream and season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Beef Stroganoff
raw_recipe.description: This easy beef stroganoff recipe with ground beef is made rich and creamy with sour cream and mushroom soup and ready to serve in under 30 minutes.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make a simple Beef Stroganoff in this easy-to-follow recipe video. Perfect for busy weeknights, this dish combines tender beef strips with a creamy, savory mushroom sauce.

review.reviewBody: This is good, but wanted to pass along this hint: try adding a package of DRY HIDDEN VALLEY RANCH dressing mix to it... oh my gosh - it is SO GOOD!

This recipe was really quick and easy to make, but tasted great...after reading other's suggestions, and catering to my family's taste, these are the modifications I made:
- chop up and onion and throw it in with the beef while it's cooking (next time I will use two for more onion)
- after draining beef, double the mushroom soup, add two cans of slice mushrooms, and add one soup can of milk
- i added about a cup of sour cream, don't worry if people don't like it, my sister hates it, and mixed in with the other ingredients, it tasted great
The extra soup and milk really made a nice sauce so when I served it over egg noodles, everything was coated perfectly. Thanks for an awesome recipe!

YUMMY! I altered the recipe a bit after looking at the other reviews. Cook the ground beef and drain off the fat. To the beef, add 1 cup of water, 2 beef boullion cubes, 1 Tbsp. dried minced onion, 1 Tbsp. Worstershire sauce, 1 tsp. crushd garlic, and a can of condensed cream of mushroom soup. Simmer for 10-20 minutes while cooking the pasta. Add 1/2 cup of sour cream to the beef and serve it over the cooked pasta.

Been making this for years it is quick & easy what I do different is use a can of cr. of Mushroom & cream of celery, use garlic salt, onion and 2 tablespoons of cooking sherry and a cup or so of sour cream. I think the sherry gives it that something some are looking for.

It’s great! If you read some reviews and they say it’s bland it’s your job as a cook to salt and pepper. I did change it up a little, I did the following: better than bouillon, added to the raw ground meat used Italian seasoning, and finished with parsley. Thanks to those home cooks for some of those suggestions.

Simple. I used beef tips and added onion and mushrooms to tips as they cooked. Added a bit of paprika, cayenne pepper (we love heat) and a splash of Worcestershire to cream of mushroom sauce as it simmered....DELICIOUS

I've made this recipe for years but with a few things that will elevate this much higher. In addition to this I also add a few tablespoons of Dijon mustard and a few tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce. I also add lots of fresh mushrooms, garlic and shallots. Topped with fresh parsley
This was so easy to make and we loved it. I did add 1/4 cup milk when I added the soup. My ground beef was 95/5%, so it needed a bit more liquid and the milk did just the trick.

To make the recipe more flavorful, I added sauteed baby bella mushrooms, onions and garlic to the ground beef. I also seasoned the ground beef with pepper and other spices. Once I added the soup, I added a teaspoon of beef bouilion to the ground beef mixture.

As most of all the other reviews indicate, this is a great starter recipe that you can customize easily. I read a lot reviews before I made it and I’m glad I did. My takeaway is to add the Worcester sauce and hidden valley ranch powder pack many suggested. I also added 1/2 can of milk and 1/2 can of beef broth and sautéed minced garlic in butter before adding the hamburger. I didn’t use any garlic powder. The amount the recipe calls for is way too much.

I made this and added a lot of different seasonings (little chili powder, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper, and parsley) it was a good recipe and the only changes I added was using 2 cans on cream of mushroom and a little water (2 cups)because it didn't have a whole lot of moisture in it. When you reheat for left overs, add water, I reheated it on the stove and it worked like a charm!
It’s fast, easy and everyone loves it. I add 8oz chopped mushrooms to the recipe
This is a great recipe .. There wasn't a drop leftover!!! I Will keep this one in my weekly rotation!!!
Came out not saucy enough and very bland. Even with salt and pepper added, it needed more sauce and flavor.
I used stirfry beef instead of ground beef
I added Worcester sauce because it was too bland. It was easy to put together.
No flavor to this recipe. Will jot make it again.
I added worcestershire to ground beef while it was cooking. Also added a package of lipton onion soup mix instead of chopping onions.

I made it before per recipe it was a hit with my family, I use ground turkey This time I used a prepared brown gravy I always use garlic so 1 sm clove minced and tossed in a bag of frozen sweet peas defrosted n drained when adding noodles to meat, the heat from both heated peas immediately while cooling down meal so I was able to serve dinner with no waiting-wonderful not asked numerous times that question how long to eat or it’s done why do we have to wait! Served with salad

I have been making an almost identical dish to this for over 50 years. I use Cream of Chicken soup, add fresh sliced and sautéed mushrooms and onions, and top with parsley. One of my absolute favorite meals!
